text:
sam: Quick thread — I ran a focused perf sweep across Mixtral-8x7b and Qwen-7B on the paged-kv branch, found a nasty throughput regression when num_key_value_heads is mismatched with attention heads. results attached below. :eyes:

alex: ok, dump the numbers pls

sam: Mixtral-8x7b (baseline contiguous KV): tokens/s steady-state ~ 5,200 at seq=1k, batch=8. With paged KV + num_kv_heads=8 (attn_heads=16) tokens/s dropped to ~4,480 (-14%).

joel: the mismatch ring a bell — fragmentation and higher scatter/gather overhead on GPU?

sam: Exactly. Profiling shows a lot more small GPU memcpy ops around page boundaries. nvprof snippet: 
```
GPU memcpy HtoD  3.2ms x 128
GPU memcpy DtoH  0.4ms x 384
kernel: kv_read_page   0.08ms x 7600
kernel: kv_unshuffle  0.12ms x 7600
```

ria: Were you running MQA or GQA configuration?

sam: GQA on Mixtral run. We tried a GQA->MQA swap for Qwen to test per-head kv dims. Qwen-7B (MQA style, num_kv_heads per shard = 4, attn_heads=16) had better memory footprint but similar fragmentation unless kv_dim aligned to head_dim.

anita: Can you paste the config block you used?

sam: Sure:
```
{
  "model": "mixtral-8x7b",
  "layout": "paged",
  "num_key_value_heads": 8,
  "num_attention_heads": 16,
  "kv_dim": 64,
  "page_size_kv": 32768,
  "kernel_policy": "auto",
  "batching": { "max_tokens": 32768, "min_batch_size": 2 }
}
```

alex: Interesting page_size_kv is small. Maybe page granularity triggers extra metadata ops. Did you try increasing page_size_kv?

sam: Yes — bumping page_size_kv to 131072 recovered ~7% throughput but not all. Root cause looks twofold: 1) non-power-of-two kv_dim/head_dim misalignment causes per-page re-packing kernels to run, 2) extra scatter for GQA when num_kv_heads != num_attn_heads.

joel: For kernel selection, we saw fused_kv_unshuffle helps when head_dim <= 64. For head_dim 128/256, we fallback to block GEMM and the overhead is acceptable. Did the auto policy pick fused kernels?

sam: Auto picked fused for kv_unshuffle but the runtime still launched additional small read kernels because pages were stored per-kv-head instead of contiguous across heads. That mixing caused repeated unshuffle calls per page.

ria: What about RoPE scaling? Any impact there?

sam: Yes — larger RoPE scaling (for long-range configs) increased per-token compute a bit but the real issue was precision noise when we quantized KV to 4-bit in MQA. RoPE interpolation + 4-bit causes small dot-prod variance that forced slight softmax shifts, increasing beam instability in evals.

anita: Did you profile cache hit rates?

sam: Hit-rate graph: contiguous layout (GQA): 94% prefix KV hits for typical RLHF prefixes. paged layout (in current impl): 76% effective hits due to page fragmentation and overfetch. Still, cache memory usage dropped 28%.

alex: So tradeoff: lower memory vs throughput/quality. Any quick wins?

sam: A few action items from the sweep:
- align num_key_value_heads to be a divisor of num_attention_heads where possible (or make runtime remap logical heads to physical pages)
- increase page_size_kv for long-seq workloads to reduce per-page overhead
- add a contiguous-hot-path: if last N layers have full-head-range access pattern, read contiguous KV for those layers and keep paged for colder layers
- extend fused kernels to handle head_dim multiples (64*2) to avoid fallbacks
- add a small batching heuristic: if avg seq_len>512 use aggressive batching but cap max_batch_latency at 80ms to avoid latency spikes

joel: Can we add a runtime patch to detect severe fragmentation and auto-fallback to contiguous layout for that request?

sam: Yes — prototype: at request time compute estimated pages_to_touch = ceil((seq_len*kv_dim*num_kv_heads)/page_size_kv). If pages_to_touch > threshold (say 12) then force sequential contiguous read via a temp gather kernel. That reduced page memcopies by ~60% in sim runs.

ria: Any perf regressions tied to kernel selection changes from last week? We merged kernel v2 which added a sync in kv_unshuffle.

sam: Kernel v2 introduced an extra cudaStreamSynchronize when switching kernels. That hurt some small-batch latency at p95. Reverted the sync in a hotfix branch and p95 returned to baseline. We'll push a test that fails if any kernel adds a blocking sync.

anita: For MQA sizing — what's the recommended num_kv_heads and kv_dim to keep both quality and throughput?

sam: For Qwen-7B we found sweet spot: num_kv_heads=16 (equal to attn heads), kv_dim=64 per head, layout=contiguous for early layers, paged for deeper layers. For Mixtral micro-variants where head_dim=128, use fused kernels with kv_dim=128 and page_size_kv=131072.

perf-bot: New perf artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/mqagqa/1765001122/sweep.tar.gz :white_check_mark:

alex: I'll pull the artifacts and try the contiguous-hot-path in my local repro. If it moves the needle we'll add a toggle in runtime flags.

joel: Also add telemetry: pages_touched_per_request, avg_unshuffle_calls, kv_memcpy_ms. Those will help triage in prod if customers see regressions.

sam: Agreed. I'll open a PR with the detection heuristic + telemetry + kernel sync revert. Assigning to @joel for kernel tests and @alex for layout tests.

ria: tagging eng-sre for canary rollout plan? @eng-sre? :bell:

anita: Nice work — this explains a lot of the 10–15% perf noise we saw on dedicated pools last week.

sam: TL;DR: mismatch in num_key_value_heads vs attention heads + small page_size + kernel sync created fragmentation and small-kernel overhead. Short-term: increase page_size, revert sync, add pages_to_touch heuristic. Mid-term: smarter remapping and extended fused-kernel support.

alex: thanks — I'll report back with canary numbers. :thumbsup:
